original_question: Consider the following properties of the generation A of a C0 -semigroups (T (t))t≥0 . (i) rg A closed. (ii) rg(1 − T (t)) closed for one t > 0. Does assertion (ii) imply assertion (i)?
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right open problem almost exactly: it involves a C0-semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} with generator A, compares the closedness of Ran(A) with the closedness of Ran(I−T(t)) for a single positive time t, and asks whether property (ii) implies property (i). That is precisely the implication asked in the paper.
missing_details: The ambient space X should be stated explicitly: A is the generator of a C0-semigroup on a Banach space X.
The operator in (ii) should be written as I−T(t), with I the identity operator on X.
The notation 'rg' should be expanded or clarified as the operator range Ran(·).
It should be stated that 'closed' means closed in X.
The quantifier in (ii) is existential: there exists t0>0 such that Ran(I−T(t0)) is closed.
No extra assumptions such as boundedness of the semigroup, analyticity, contractivity, or Hilbert-space structure appear in the paper; these should not be added.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space, let (T(t))_{t≥0} be a C0-semigroup on X with generator A, and suppose that there exists t0>0 such that Ran(I−T(t0)) is closed in X. Must Ran(A) be closed in X?
justification: The draft is a near-verbatim restatement of the paper’s Problem 25 in Section 7. The paper asks exactly whether closedness of the range of I−T(t) for one positive time implies closedness of the range of the generator A. The only nearby contextual addition in the paper is the comment that this is a version of a spectral inclusion theorem and that the converse implication does not hold. Since the paper gives the problem in this narrow form and does not add further hypotheses, the refined version should remain equally narrow and only make the ambient Banach space, the identity operator, and the quantifier in (ii) explicit.
